done.why: The parser rejected most of my odd phrasings, and the Carousel Room's exits were blocked by rockfalls, so I saw no goal ahead.

about: A Zork-style underground cave. You start in a barrow with a lantern and an Elvish sword, then cross a bridge into a great cavern. Beyond that are a formal garden with a unicorn and a disorienting carousel room. A wizard roams and casts spells on you.

moments.note: Take everything reported each item separately and tidily.
I tried 'go down' on the bridge and got 'The drop would be fatal.' Then a wizard appeared, cast Fantasize and vanished.
The basilisk's description and presence vanished from the room with no explanation. Later a grue stood where it had been.
Examine, attack, kill and x were all 'not recognized', even for a creature listed in the room.
I walked into the dark place without a lamp and was not eaten after waiting twice.
The sword glowed in the garden when the unicorn and wizards were near, and stopped when the unicorn left.
The Carousel Room disorients you, and the rockfall messages on its exits were wry.

wished: Examine creatures and scenery such as the basilisk, wizards and gazebo.
Phrase requests more freely, such as asking politely or combining items.
Be told what the Wizard's spell actually did.

lines.why: A curt refusal followed by a wizard's sudden appearance made the world feel alive.

lines.line: The passage south is choked with a fall of rock not far in. Whatever lies beyond it will have to wait.
lines.why: Blocked exits with a wry promise of later content.

fun.why: Some charming touches, but the parser was narrow and my odd inputs mostly failed.

engagement.why: Exploring was easy and the wizard and glowing sword intrigued me, but blocked paths slowed things.

difficulty.why: Navigation was easy, but the verbs were hard to guess.

interestingness.why: Familiar cave locations mixed with a wizard's spell effects that change the world.

prose.why: Clean, evocative room descriptions and good dry humor.
